title: MAGE query and query result
description: A question asked of a model system, and the shape of the answer. Every query carries an explicit quantifier: it determines what counts as evidence, and conflating existential with universal is the error the workbench exists to make visible. Semantics in SEMANTICS.md section 7.

name.description: Human-facing question. Saved queries re-run on model change.

expect.description: Expected outcome, for a saved query used as a CI gate. Present means the query is an ASSERTION: a run whose outcome differs is a build failure. Absent means the query is exploratory and any outcome is reported without judgement. Values are holds/refuted/... and never true/false -- a bare boolean here is a YAML-coercion bug (V25).

quantifier.description: exists: a witness proves TRUE, exhaustive absence proves FALSE. forall: exhaustive satisfaction proves TRUE, a counterexample proves FALSE. Never inferred silently -- an ambiguous natural-language question triggers Clarification or a displayed interpretation (V21).

behaviorQuery.description: A question about executions. Safety and reachability only: fairness is unsupported, so 'can it reach X' is in scope and 'will it eventually reach X' is not.

form.description: reach: a configuration satisfying target is reachable. invariant: predicate holds in every reachable configuration. recurrence: the target is RE-ENTERED -- a target configuration, at least one step, another target configuration; evidence is a LASSO whose cycle is the target-to-target segment. repeatable-cycle: a genuinely repeated CONFIGURATION, which is what makes a cycle actually repeatable; a loop whose bounded variable strictly advances answers refuted here while recurrence answers holds. Two forms, because can-it-come-back and can-it-loop-indefinitely are different questions and a query must denote a question rather than a search strategy. deadend: a configuration with no enabled step exists. transition-live: a named transition is executable in some reachable configuration.

target.description: State predicate. Required for reach and recurrence.

predicate.description: State predicate asserted to hold. Required for invariant.

avoid.description: Configurations the trace must never pass through. A past-time question is NOT expressed here -- it compiles to an invariant over a history variable, and the compilation is disclosed (V23).

limit.description: Max configurations to explore. Exceeding it yields coverage.kind=bounded, and therefore result=inconclusive (V22) -- never 'no'.

predicate.description: Conjunction of atoms unless all-of/any-of/not is used. An atom's key names a machine state (document.state), an instance state (worker[1].state), a variable, or a derived value.

quantityQuery.description: A quantitative question. There is deliberately NO aggregation parameter: the aggregation is DERIVED from the metric's dimension scope (SEMANTICS.md section 8) -- latency and cost are worst-case sums along executions, peak_memory is the maximum of memory(c) over reachable configurations -- so the max|min|named selector the section 29 refinement rejected cannot reappear here. `target` selects WHICH executions (those reaching it); `within` names the declared model:-targeted ceiling to decide against. A target on a configuration-scoped metric is a category error, refused by name. With `within` the quantifier must be forall (a ceiling claim is universal); without it, exists (a measurement is established by the witness that attains it). The computed figure travels on result.magnitude, dimension attached.

metric.description: The analysis, not a dimension: latency and cost account executions under the declared basis (V35); peak_memory is memory(c)'s reachable maximum. Kept in parity with REQUIREMENT_METRICS in src/quant/requirement.ts by test/quant-query.test.ts.

target.description: Execution-scoped metrics only: measure the executions REACHING a configuration satisfying this predicate. On a configuration-scoped metric this is a category error, refused rather than computed.

within.description: The model:-targeted quantity declaring the ceiling to decide against. A name that resolves to no declared quantity is a V39 finding at authoring time and a refusal at ask time.

limit.description: Max configurations to explore. Exceeding it yields coverage.kind=bounded, and therefore result=inconclusive (V22).

relation.description: Relation type traversed. A multi-hop form over a type with composition.path=forbidden is REFUSED, not answered (V7) -- outcome=unlicensed.

where.description: Join predicate over endpoint properties, e.g. source.classification > target.accepts. Well-typed only if both sides declare the SAME ordered domain (V20).

outcome.description: holds: the claim is established (a witness for exists, exhaustive satisfaction for forall). refuted: the claim is refuted (exhaustive absence for exists, a counterexample for forall). inconclusive: mandatory when coverage is bounded (V22). unlicensed: the model does not authorize the question -- a SUCCESSFUL result, not an error (V7, V24). Deliberately NOT true/false: there is no boolean result, only a claim plus coverage plus evidence -- and a bare `true`/`false` in YAML is implicit-typed to a boolean anyway (V25).

interpreted-as.description: The question actually evaluated, in plain language. Mandatory when the query came from natural language (V21).

formal-query.description: The query object actually executed. The UI exposes this beside the answer.

magnitude.description: The figure a quantity query computed -- a worst-case total or a peak -- in the BASE unit of its dimension. The dimension travels WITH the number for the reason the RDF projection keeps it: a bare number lets a consumer add milliseconds to megabytes, which V30 forbids at the validation layer. Null/absent on non-quantitative results, and when a maximum is unbounded (the lasso evidence is the answer then).

unit.description: The dimension's base unit; null when the dimension is dimensionless.

refusal.description: Why the model does not license the question, as the sentence a person reads. Required when outcome=unlicensed. The same fact as data travels in refusalDetail; the two are written by one constructor and cannot disagree.

compilation.description: Disclosed rewrites, e.g. an auxiliary history variable added to answer a past-time question (V23).

evidence.description: A witness supports an existential; a counterexample refutes a universal. A lasso is required for recurrence.

cycle.description: The repeating suffix. Required when shape=lasso.

machines.description: Instances that moved. More than one means a declared synchronized event fired.

refusalReason.description: The closed cause vocabulary every refusal carries (result.refusalDetail.reason, and the refusal arm of check()). A refusal is a SUCCESSFUL outcome (V7): composition-forbidden: the relation type declares composition.path forbidden (V7). missing-distinction: the model represents the subject but deliberately omits what the question needs (V24). unknown-vocabulary: the question names an entity, state, variable or relation this system does not declare. missing-model-type: the system declares no substrate of the model type the question interrogates. unsupported-form: the form exists in this schema but this version does not evaluate it. quantifier-mismatch: the declared quantifier asks for evidence the form cannot produce (section 7). unsupported-expression: an effect or derived expression outside the deliberately tiny grammars. reserved-feature: legal to write, reserved for a future version, refused rather than misread (V14/V15). category-error: the question pairs a quantity with the aggregation axis its scope does not have (section 8). Mirrors REFUSAL_REASONS in src/ir/types.ts; the parity is test-held in both directions.

refusalDetail.description: The refusal's typed half: the cause as data, beside the sentence in result.refusal. An agent branches on reason; missing lists the distinctions the model would need in order to answer (empty when the gap is not a modeling one); models lists the models consulted while deciding, so a caller can say where to add the distinction.

modelType.description: The model-type registry's closed id vocabulary -- the modelType a check() report names in its licensed arm, and the type each query kind interrogates: structural-graph answers kind=graph (the graphQuery forms), state-machine answers kind=behavior (the behaviorQuery forms), quantitative-model answers kind=quantity (the quantityQuery metrics).

binding.description: The closed binding-name vocabulary: every declared correspondence between elements in different purposeful models, and the names the composed view's focus accepts. appears-in: one entity's identity across the purposeful models that mention it (entity-model). machine-of-entity: this behavioural model describes this structural entity (machine-entity). state-of-entity: an entity property naming the lifecycle state during whose occupancy it runs (entity-state).

querySubject.description: What a question may be ABOUT, per model type: the registry's closed {noun, selector} pairs. The selector names the grammar that picks instances of the noun out: by-id takes a declared identifier; property-constraints takes a {property: value | {ne} | {in: []}} object; predicate takes a predicate over machine state; selector takes a partial match on declared transition fields (machine/from/to/sync). A name outside the declared vocabulary is an invalid question, not evidence of absence.
